hero.description: I build scalable, accessible, and high-performance web applications with React and TypeScript, using an AI-driven workflow with Claude, MCP, and coding agents. This lets me ship features faster, modernize legacy code, and automate testing while delivering great user experiences.

about.title: About Me
about.description1: Senior Frontend-focused Fullstack Engineer with 15+ years of experience building scalable, accessible web applications with React, Next.js, TypeScript and Angular, backed by Node.js/Fastify, REST APIs and C#/.NET backends. Strong in frontend architecture, design systems and performance, with a track record of modernising legacy codebases and turning UI/UX designs into production-ready products. Experienced in taking applications end to end, from code to production: containerising with Docker, deploying to Kubernetes on AWS EKS with Helm, managing infrastructure as code with Terraform, and automating releases with CI/CD pipelines. Works AI-first day to day — using Claude, AI coding agents and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to speed up delivery, automate workflows and raise code quality — and builds AI-powered products such as OFPLens, an AI flight-briefing app with evals to verify LLM accuracy.
about.description2: When I'm not coding, you can find me exploring new technologies, creating cinematic videos and animations, contributing to Stack Overflow, or sharing knowledge with the developer community

featured.title: Featured Project
featured.tagline: A fullstack AI-powered app for aviation enthusiasts that turns an official flight plan (OFP) into a clear briefing.
featured.point1: Route data, weather forecasts, an AI-generated briefing and a map view with hazards along the route.
featured.point2: AI briefing pipeline built with Claude, with evals that measure briefing accuracy against the source data.
featured.point3: Containerised with Docker and deployed on Kubernetes (AWS EKS) with Helm, with infrastructure as code in Terraform and CI/CD for automated builds and deployments. The beta is torn down nightly and recreated on demand to keep cloud costs low.
